title: Placeholder: moles in a weighed sample

stimulus.title: A weighed sample
stimulus.text: A student weighs 22.0 g of carbon dioxide (molar mass 44.01 g/mol).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the number of moles of carbon dioxide in the sample.
parts.sample: 22.0 g × (1 mol / 44.01 g) = 0.500 mol of carbon dioxide.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the number of molecules in the sample.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A second student reports 968 mol. Explain the error and how an estimate would have caught it.

rubric.point: Names the error: multiplied by the molar mass instead of dividing
Estimate: 22 g is about half of 44 g, so about 0.5 mol

parts.sample: The student multiplied the mass by the molar mass (22.0 × 44.01 = 968). The sample weighs about half of 44 g, so it should be about half a mole, which shows 968 is far too large.
